title: talk-to-assistant — the box you type or speak into reaches the Servex assistant, on the Prompts tab

set.request: so, is there a fast assistant i can talk to via the browser? where do i click? -- the typed box should reach the Servex assistant and live at the top of the Prompts tab, not just voice.
set.now: reading compose.js, Dictate.js, prompts.js, page.js's now_view
steps: read compose.js, Dictate.js, prompts.js, the now_view mount site
decide the shared-helper shape for posting a prompt to Servex
lift post_prompt() out of Dictate.js, reuse it in Dictate and compose
compose.js: send() posts to Servex first, falls back to the old stream
mount composer() at the top of the Prompts tab, scroll to new row on live arrivals
note line under the box + v3.css touch-up for the top-of-tab spot
node --check every edited file, reload hold, headless proof at 8098
screenshot: real send with Servex up, and the dead-port fallback
set.outcome:
**Typed words now reach the fast assistant.** The box that used to only stream to the old one-shot assistant preset now posts straight to Servex's `/log/prompts` (`{type: "prompt", by: "owner", text, via: "typed"}`), falling back to the old stream only when Servex is not answering — never both. The SAME box now lives at the top of the Prompts tab, above the thread, mounted a second time there alongside the Now tab it already had, and the Prompts tab scrolls to the newest row as each name/card lands. The note under the box always reads "the fast assistant inside Servex · names in ~2 s · ✓ ✗ optional", swapping in "sent to the assistant" or "Servex is down — old assistant" for a few seconds after every send. Proven headless at 400 and 1280 on a private port: a real send named itself within three seconds with zero uncaught JS errors, and pointing the base at a dead test port showed the fallback note with zero uncaught JS errors too (the browser's own network log for a genuinely dead test port still shows two `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` lines — unavoidable, not a code defect, detailed in the task log). Left alone on purpose: `page.js` needed no edit at all, since `prompts_view()` already owns its own DOM — so it was never touched, honoring the concurrent servex-hardening edit there.
